summary: `bun create blueshed/paintbrush` has been run from a local template only, not from the GitHub tarball
detail: bun create runs the postinstall for GitHub and local templates alike (Bun's docs). The flow was run from a local template (BUN_CREATE_DIR) on Bun 1.4.2: the postinstall ran, the new app named itself, copied railroad's skills, dropped create/, the logo and the template ledger, and its own typecheck and tests passed at 100%. The GitHub path (tarball download, then the same steps) was not run, because the branch is not on main yet. After it is merged, run bun create blueshed/paintbrush into a scratch folder, and bun test in it.

summary: The parts were each applied to a scratch copy and run, but nothing in this repo fails if one goes stale
detail: The static-files, WebSocket, SQLite and passwords parts were applied to a copy of the template (27 tests at 100%), and the live-documents part was applied from its own code blocks to another (17 tests at 100%, a second window sees a save, typing is not overwritten). That run found a real flaw: the SQLite part's refusal test did not send a body that is not JSON, so the route's .catch(() => null) was an uncovered function and bun test failed the gate. The recipes are prose, so a change in delta, railroad or Bun would only show when someone applies one. Consider a test that applies each part to a scratch copy and runs it, in CI.

summary: A new app's first commit can miss .claude/skills, because bun create commits while the postinstall is still running
detail: Seen once on Bun 1.4.2 with a local template: the initial commit held everything setup.ts had written except the skills it copies last, so git status in the new app shows .claude/skills/ untracked; a later run had them all. The files on disk are right. Bun's docs say the git step runs on its own thread. A fix would wait for the commit and amend it, guarded so it never amends a commit that is not bun create's (its message is 'Initial commit (via bun create)'). Not done: it is machinery for a first git add.

summary: duckdown's bun-create postinstall is "bun run create/setup.ts", which bun create runs with a second `bun run` in front: nothing happens
detail: Found building paintbrush's create script. bun create prefixes every postinstall entry with `bun run`, so an entry that starts with `bun run` does nothing, silently. Checked on Bun 1.4.2 by running duckdown's own create from a local copy (BUN_CREATE_DIR): the created site kept the template's todo.jsonl and create/, and had no site/. The entry that works is create/setup.ts. The GitHub path was not run, but Bun's docs say it shares the steps. duckdown's ledger and README are the home for this; it is noted here so the finding is not lost.
